newsitem.title: MEXICO: Banobras to place $200 to $400 mln in bonds in '97.
newsitem.headline: Banobras to place $200 to $400 mln in bonds in '97.

text.p: Mexican development bank, Banco Nacional de Obras y Servicios Publico (Banobras), will place between $200 million and $400 million in bonds in international markets this year, the bank's director general said on Monday.
"This year we will go again to international markets, and are thinking about around $200 to $400 million," said Jaime Corredor Esnaola at a news conference.
He did not give a specific date for the issue.
The bank said the issue would be similar to that placed last November, when it placed a $200 million seven-year issue, with a coupon of 9.625 percent.
He also said that Banobras could take part in issuing debt for the planned Mexican pension system, the Afores.
"We hope that within the internal market we can participate even more, in the setting up of the Afores," he said.
"Without doubt Banobras will try to obtain a part of the resources placed with the Afores," he added.
He noted the development bank remained financially sound.
